subject: E-Commerce
title: What Are Dark Patterns?
description: A 60-second lesson on What Are Dark Patterns?.

hook.text: Dark patterns are design tricks that manipulate you into doing things you didn't intend. Every major site uses them.

buildup.text: Harry Brignull coined the term in 2010. He catalogued sneaky UI tricks that exploit user psychology.

discovery.text: Pre-checked boxes, hidden unsubscribe buttons, and confusing opt-outs are all classic dark patterns.

twist.text: The EU's GDPR and California's laws now ban some dark patterns. Regulators are catching up.

climax.text: Dark patterns work because they exploit fast, automatic thinking. Slowing down defeats most of them.

punchline.text: Every major site uses them. Dark patterns profit from your autopilot brain.

quiz.question: What are dark patterns in e-commerce?
options: Design tricks that manipulate users into unintended actions
